thread:
Jordan: Heads-up: we're shipping a change to regional SLO tiers and running a tail-sensitive loadtest this Friday 22:00-23:30 UTC. Scope: routing control plane + serving pools in eu-west and us-west.
Priya: Quick summary of policy change?
Jordan: Two things: 1) introduce "SLO tier 2" for high-throughput routes with P95 target instead of P99 for peak windows; 2) add an automated circuit-breaker that trips on rapid P99 jumps (configurable). This is a conservative rollout.
Ethan: What's the rollout schedule? Full or staged?
Jordan: Staged. Friday test is stage 0 (dry-run with synthetic clients). If all good, we'll enable on a subset of routes Mon 00:00 UTC for 24h.
Nina: Any customer-facing notices?
Jordan: No consumer outage planned. We'll post a note to status page and email enterprise contacts for affected tenants.
SRE-Bot: Ticket RI-2026-341 created; CR attached.
Priya: Test plan bullets?
Jordan: Test plan: 
- 22:00: enable synthetic heavy-tail traffic to eu-west (rload config attached)
- 22:15: flip circuit-breaker to monitor-only (no enforced reroute)
- 22:45: enable breaker in enforcement mode for us-west subset (10% traffic)
- 23:10: scale serving pools down/up to simulate spot reclaim and watch fallback routing
- 23:25: tear-down and short smoke test
Allow 5-10m observation between steps.
Ethan: Post-test metrics we'll collect?
Jordan: p50/p95/p99, error rate, fallback rate, model-variant fallback counts, KV cache miss ratio, autoscaler events, and per-tenant latencies.
Nina: Rollback criteria?
Jordan: Rollback and force-stop if any of:
- sustained P99 > 400ms for >3m on any primary route
- absolute error rate >1% for >2m
- breaker side-effects causing >2% traffic drop to healthy backends
If triggered, run `scripts/cb/disable_breaker_all.sh` and `scripts/routing/revert_partial.sh <region>`. Notify product and account ops.
Priya: Can you paste the rload command we'll use?
Jordan: Sure:
```
rload --target https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate --qps 350 --tail 99 --duration 1800s --payloads heavy-tail-prompts.json
```
Ethan: What's `--tail 99`? New flag?
Jordan: It's a client flag that biases request patterns to long-context prompts to stress KV and batching behavior.
SRE-Bot: Synthetic monitor `tail-check-eu-west` scheduled every 15s for the window.
Oncall Rotation: Primary for window: Priya, Secondary: Ethan, Tertiary: Nina. Night backup: Jordan.
Priya: I'll watch P99 dashboards and the breaker logs. I set an alert to notify #eng-oncall if p99 rises 150ms above baseline.
Nina: I'll handle status updates and the enterprise notify list.
Ethan: I'll run correlation scripts post-step: `tools/correlate_tail_anomalies --since now-30m --dest s3://ops-artifacts/tailtest/1789012345`
Jordan: Reminder: during the enforcement step the system may reroute to quantized variants. Keep an eye on unit-cost and semantic drift.
Priya: Noted. Also disable scheduled model rollouts during the window (patch in release calendar).
Nina: Calendar invites sent.
SRE-Bot: Reminder 30m until start.
Ethan: Acknowledged. I'll be on standby 21:45->23:45 UTC.
Jordan: Thanks. Post-mortem draft if anything happens: use the short-template and ping me for reviewer assignment. Keep messages tight and include metric snippets.
Priya: Copy.
Nina: :thumbsup:
Ethan: :white_check_mark:
